subject: Clarify: Use of customer data for model training & deletion timelines
messages:
From: Rajesh Patel <security@finbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on model training & deletion — FinBank info

Hi Soojin,

Quick Q from our InfoSec review: your standard answers state 'Redwood does not train models on customer data' — could you provide a short written assurance for our security team that explains: whether customer prompt/content may ever be used to train or fine-tune public models, how long input content and generated output are retained, what happens to backups and logs, and the deletion turnaround once requested?

A few specifics we need for procurement:
- Are there any telemetry/event logs that contain customer content tokens?
- Do you retain any data in backups for >30 days?
- If we require contractual prohibition on using our content for model improvement, do you offer an addendum or config that ensures this?

If you can send a short statement we can attach to the security questionnaire, that would be great.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Head of Security Operations, FinBank
security@finbank.com

On May 10, 2026 at 11:03 AM, Soojin Lee wrote:
> High level answer: we do not use customer prompt or context to train or improve our public or internal models by default. There are an important set of nuances I want to confirm with Marcus before I send your team a formal statement for procurement.

Quick internal summary for the response we should provide to FinBank:

1) Core assurance (short, procurement-friendly):
   - "Redwood Inference will not use customer-provided content (prompts, files, or generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood-owned public models without explicit, written consent from the customer."

2) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private nuance:
   - Hosted API (default): telemetry for service operation is collected (latency, success/failure, anonymized usage metrics). We do NOT include raw customer content in model training runs. Customers may opt into sharing anonymized examples for product improvement via an explicit opt-in toggle; this is separate from required telemetry.
   - Dedicated (reserved capacity): by contract, Dedicated tenants have an opt-out by default for training; we can add a clause that prohibits data usage for model improvement.
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): customer controls the environment and Redwood does not have access to customer content for training.

3) Retention and deletion specifics (recommended wording):
   - "Customer content (customer inputs and generated outputs) is retained for up to 30 days by default to support debugging, short-term analytics, and KV/prefix cache for ongoing sessions. Customers can request deletion of their content at any time; deletion requests will be processed within 7 business days and confirmed in writing. Backups that contain customer content are retained for up to 90 days and are subject to the same deletion request process (we will purge from backups within 90 days, with best-effort expedited purge where feasible)."

4) Logs and telemetry:
   - Operational logs may contain metadata (request id, model used, latency) but do not contain customer content tokens. Exception: if a customer explicitly enables detailed logging for debugging and grants permission, we may collect additional logs for troubleshooting; these are treated as customer content for retention/deletion purposes.

5) Aggregated product telemetry:
   - Aggregated, de-identified usage statistics (e.g., token volume by model family, error rates) may be used to improve product quality. These aggregates do not contain customer-identifiable content and are not used to train models on customer content.

6) Legal/contractual mechanisms:
   - We offer contract language/addendum that: (a) prohibits use of customer content for model training, (b) specifies retention windows and deletion SLAs, and (c) includes a breach notification cadence. For high-security customers we can add dedicated clauses and SOC2 evidence.

7) Exceptions and emergency debug access:
   - In rare cases (security incident, court order), Redwood may access customer content as required by law or to resolve security incidents. We notify customers per our policy unless prohibited.

Action items for Soojin:
- Send a clean procurement-ready paragraph plus the two attachments (Customer Data Use Statement + SOC2 redacted).
- Ask Legal if we need signature on the data-use statement; if yes we'll have standard SOW language or an addendum. (Neha, please advise)

Marcus
Director, Security & Compliance

Hi Rajesh — thanks for the clear list. Attached are two documents: "Redwood_Customer_Data_Use_Statement.pdf" (short procurement-ready statement) and a redacted copy of our latest SOC 2 Type II report. Summary statement below that you can paste into your questionnaire:

--- start statement ---
Redwood Inference: Customer Data Use & Retention Statement (short)

Redwood Inference will not use customer-provided content (prompts, uploaded files, or generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood-owned public models without explicit, written consent from the customer.

Retention and deletion:
- Customer content is retained for up to 30 days by default to enable debugging, short-term analytics, and session continuity.
- Backups that may contain customer content are retained for up to 90 days; we will remove content from backups within this window and will work with customers with accelerated purge requests where technically possible.
- Customers may submit deletion requests at any time. Redwood commits to processing deletion requests within 7 business days and will provide confirmation when the deletion is complete.

Telemetry and logs:
- Operational telemetry (latency, error rates, request IDs) does not include raw customer content tokens and may be used in aggregate to improve system reliability.
- Detailed logs that include customer content are only captured with customer consent (e.g., opt-in debugging) and are treated as customer content for retention and deletion.

Deployment modes:
- Hosted API: default telemetry collection is anonymized and customer content is not used for model training; customers may opt into data sharing for product improvement via explicit opt-in.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): data-use restrictions for training are enforceable by contract and can be set to a strict prohibition.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed environment; Redwood does not access or use customer content for training.

Exceptions:
- Redwood may access customer content when required by law or to investigate security incidents; we will notify customers unless legally prohibited.

For contract language, signature, or a tailored addendum, we are happy to provide standard clause wording. Please let me know if FinBank needs a signed addendum; we can route to Legal and produce a redlined addendum within 3 business days.
--- end statement ---

I have also included links to the HubSpot record for your procurement ticket and a Drive folder with the supporting docs. If FinBank needs any small edits to the statement (shorter/longer or different phrasing for the questionnaire), tell me where it will be pasted and we can adapt.
